raw_block.rationale: Create a narrowly scoped §3306(c)(5) helper so family-employment claims are evaluated under the applicable family-relationship rule instead of the unrelated domestic-service rule. A categorical relationship input also permits short-circuit evaluation when the worker's age is absent but an unconditionally covered relationship is known.

inputs.name: employer_relationship_to_worker
inputs.question: What family relationship of the employing person to the individual performing the service is stated in the current facts, expressed as son, daughter, spouse, father, mother, or none?

inputs.name: worker_age
inputs.question: What age of the individual performing the service is expressly stated in the current facts?

inputs.name: question_asserts_section_applies
inputs.question: Does the current question affirm, rather than deny, that section 3306(c)(5) applies to the described service?

skill.intent: Determine whether a claim that 26 U.S.C. §3306(c)(5) applies to service performed in a specified family employment relationship is entailed or contradicted.

outputs.description: The current native answer label: Entailment if the asserted applicability matches §3306(c)(5), otherwise Contradiction.
outputs.name: answer

support.text: Alice has paid $3200 to her father Bob for work done from Feb 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2017, in Baltimore, Maryland, USA.
Section 3306(c)(5) applies to Alice employing Bob for the year 2017.

In the case of domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages in cash of $1,000 or more for such service.
(3) Domestic service

In the case of domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages in cash of $1,000 or more for such service.
